title: Software Engineer - Developer Experience
description:
Headquarters: Portugal - Remote

Be Part of Building the Future

Dremio is the unified lakehouse platform for self-service analytics and AI, serving hundreds of global enterprises, including Maersk, Amazon, Regeneron, NetApp, and S&P Global. Customers rely on Dremio for cloud, hybrid, and on-prem lakehouses to power their data mesh, data warehouse migration, data virtualization, and unified data access use cases. Based on open source technologies, including Apache Iceberg and Apache Arrow, Dremio provides an open lakehouse architecture enabling the fastest time to insight and platform flexibility at a fraction of the cost.  Learn more at  www.dremio.com.

About the role

In this role you will get opportunities to implement and maintain CI/CD systems and developer productivity solutions. You will be responsible for both regularly scheduled work as well as on-demand break-fix work to support Dremio’s CI/CD system, identifying areas of improvement, and implementing changes to increase efficiency and effectiveness of those systems.

Bring your industry experience to improve the efficiency and scale of Dremio’s infrastructure via innovation on tooling and methodologies. You should have empathy for developers and a passion for engineering productivity.

What you’ll be doing

- Solve problems for fellow Dremio engineers by:

- Leveraging and contributing to playbooks to implement solutions to unblock them

- Identifying short term workarounds and documenting them

- Automating processes where manual processes exist.

- Working on infrastructure across all major clouds (AWS, GCP, Azure).

- Managing access to key infrastructure.

- Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines and associated systems to increase organizational efficiency.

- Automate local development workflows.

- Analyze performance bottlenecks, root cause issues, file defects, follow up with developers, and document resolutions.

- Clear focus on keeping our development branches ‘green’.

- Release engineering - automating processes to push software to delivery endpoints.

- Report out on the status, reliability and robustness of our CI/CD systems.

- Actively participate in code reviews.

What we’re looking for

- B.S. or M.S in Computer Science or in a related technical field

- 1+ years of experience on large scale distributed systems

- Comfortable navigating the fast moving, unstructured nature of a hyper-growth startup.

- Demonstrable Knowledge and Experience with at least one cloud platform (AWS, Azure, GCP)

- Basic understanding of cloud networking and cloud architecture.

- Proficiency in any of Java/C++/Python/Go

- Knowledge of Maven or similar build environments

- Hands on experience in pipeline automation using CI/CD tools like Jenkins

- Experience in Infrastructure as Code

- Experience with Terraform, BASH, Docker, Jenkins, and Kubernetes

- Ability to write technical reports, effectively summarizing key data

- Passion for learning and then delivering solutions using latest technologies

- Strong Affinity for collaboration and teamwork

Bonus points if you have

- Working knowledge in data lakes and data warehousing

- Proficient with SQL

What we value

At Dremio, we hold ourselves to high standards when it comes to People, Thinking, and Action. Our Gnarlies (that's what we call our employees) communicate with clarity, drive accountability, and are respectful towards each other. We confront brutal facts and focus on results while operating with a sense of urgency and building a "flywheel". People who like to jump in and drive momentum will thrive in our #GnarlyLife.

Dremio is an equal opportunity employer supporting workforce diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, protected veteran status, disability status, or any other unlawful factor.

Dremio is committed to providing any necessary accommodations for individuals with disabilities within our application and interview process. To request accommodation due to a disability, please inform your recruiter.

Dremio has policies in place to protect the personal information that employees and applicants disclose to us. Please click here to review the privacy notice.

Important Security Notice for Candidates

At Dremio, we uphold trust and transparency as paramount values in all our interactions with customers, partners, employees, and the general public. We have been targeted by individuals creating fake domains similar to ours to scam prospects and candidates. Please note that all official communications from us will be from an @dremio.com domain. If you suspect you've been targeted by a scam, it's imperative to report the incident to your local law enforcement agencies. For more information about this type of scam, please refer to Dremio's official statement  here .

Dremio is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company that does not have a signed agreement with the Company.

title: Backend Engineer, Control Plane
description:
Headquarters: Remote (United States)

Thank you for considering Tailscale. If this job description resonates with you, please apply.  Frequently cited statistics show that people who identify with historically marginalized groups are likely to apply to jobs only if they meet 100% of the qualifications. We encourage you to help us break that statistic!

About Tailscale

Tailscale is making safe connection effortless by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. We're building a future for the Internet that's easy, sensible, and safe, like it used to be. Founded in 2019 and fully distributed, we're backed by Accel, CRV, Insight, Heavybit, and Uncork Capital.

Job Description

We’re seeking a skilled and diligent full-time Software Engineer to join our growing Control Plane Team. You will work as part of the engineering team to:

- Develop the Tailscale product, contributing to both open source client code and related backend services;

- Take ownership of the entire product lifecycle, from writing code to product ideation and strategic decision-making;

- Work closely with UX/UI designers and product managers to shape features.

Because we’re an early-stage and fully remote company, we’re looking for a strongly motivated individual who can help move the product forward at crucial intersections of the technology and organization: in this case, the control plane and the various services it comprises and supports. The ability to think on your feet, collaborate with highly technical teams, and comfort working asynchronously are essential.

Key Responsibilities

- Work as part of a team of engineers to design, build, test, and document core software components.

- Develop product features in areas that include our control plane, our relay infrastructure, and our identity integrations.

- Exhibit ownership over the running services that comprise Tailscale’s product by building for observability, participating in incident response, and fielding customer support escalations.

- Analyze and improve efficiency, scalability, and stability of various system resources.

- Bring a security-first mindset to both design and implementation.

What We Are Looking For

- Experience with distributed systems

- Experience with the Go programming language

- Experience with one or more SQL databases

- Familiarity with networking (IP addressing, routing, etc.)

- Ability to give and process constructive feedback, as well as work independently

- Flexibility to adjust to the dynamic nature of a startup

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills

As a company, we strive to maintain fair and equitable compensation practices within our team across all roles and all levels. Tailscale's compensation package includes base salary, equity, and comprehensive benefits. The salary range displayed on each job posting represents the target range for a new hire's base salary. Individual offers may vary based on experience and skill set.
US Pay Range
$163,000 — $226,000 USD

What We Offer

- An inclusive, flexible environment where you can be your authentic self. We recognize the impact of diverse voices and backgrounds on the growth of our people, product, and company. And that flexibility in how and when you work empowers our team to integrate work and life.

- A competitive total compensation package. This includes a base salary, an equity incentive plan and variable commission (for quota-based roles).

- Comprehensive group benefits with no waiting period. Take advantage of coverage for health, vision, dental, and more for you and your family!

- Remote first company —most of our teams work fully remotely. Enjoy a change of scenery wherever you can get wifi, participate in virtual and in-person social events, and leverage our corporate co-working program to visit WeWork (or other similar spaces near you). Some roles require in-office collaboration depending on team needs, which will be clearly noted in the job description.

- Employer-funded retirement contributions. Tailscale will match your retirement contributions dollar-for-dollar, up to a maximum annual employer contribution equal to 0.75% of your eligible compensation.

- Connect with other Tailscalars IRL. Attend our annual company retreat, participate in team off-sites, and collaborate in person with teammates across Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Singapore. We support intentional in-person connection through team travel and distributed collaboration.

- Support for your personal and professional development. Grow your career thoughtfully with $1500 USD annually for professional development, or take advantage of mentorship, coaching, and internal promotion opportunities.

- Paid time off and a healthy work-life integration.  Our flexible, paid time off program supports you for any situation life throws your way, whether moving homes or travelling the world!

- A build-your-own home office setup. You choose your own company-owned laptop (Mac or PC), receive a monthly home internet reimbursement, and $500 USD to customize your workstation to make it your own.

- Paid parental leave program . We care about your life outside of work and encourage new parents to take advantage of parental leave top-ups (20 weeks for birthing parents, 16 weeks for non-birthing parents).

Tailscale is committed to providing an accessible and inclusive hiring process. If you require an accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process or related to any aspect of this role, please contact your recruiter.

Our hiring process uses AI-assisted tools to help screen and assess candidates. All hiring decisions are made by people.

You would support Salesforce and the applications around it. Outreach runs sales email sequences. Gong records sales calls. Gainsight tracks customer health. Marketing Cloud sends marketing email. Salesforce is the center of the role, but you would own these applications too, learning each one on your own or through hands-on training. This is an entry-level remote role.

About the team
We are a small team in Business Systems at Veradigm . Veradigm serves physician practices, health plans and life sciences companies with software and data. We keep its Salesforce systems running and build what comes next. We support services projects on Kantata SX, quotes and contracts on Salesforce CPQ, and billing in Zuora. We also support customer cases on Service Cloud, portals on Experience Cloud, and the sales and marketing applications. Boomi connects the systems. Much of it predates the current team. We work across all of it. Nobody is tied to one product. Later we may add Service Cloud Voice, Agentforce or Revenue Cloud Advanced. So we look for people who adapt.

What you will do

- Answer support tickets and manage user access and licenses.

What we need

None of these is required.

- Experience with any of the applications above, such as Outreach, Gong, Gainsight, Marketing Cloud, LEAH or Calendly. This is a big plus.

- A Salesforce Associate, Administrator or Platform App Builder certification.

- Progress on Trailhead, Salesforce's free learning site.

- Familiarity with SQL, REST APIs or integration concepts.

The senior members of our team work remotely. You would learn from them by video call and through review of your work. Every change is reviewed before production. We use AI agents, currently Claude, to analyze, design, build, debug and troubleshoot. You would work with them and own what they produce, within company AI usage policies.

If you want to write code full time from day one, this role will frustrate you. If you enjoy learning how systems fit together, it will suit you.

title: Software Development Intern — Cloud & DevOps (AWS)
description:
This is a remote position.
Software Development Intern — Cloud & DevOps (AWS)
Trustbridge | Full-time Internship | India-based | Paid Stipend
About the Role

Trustbridge is Vulcury 's AI-enabled manufacturing supplier matching platform. Our development team is strong on core application logic but needs to build deeper strength in cloud infrastructure — specifically in using AWS to scale production workloads and replace serial processing with parallelized, cache-aware execution.
You'll start on our matching engine, where we currently make repeated, serial calls against a large historical project corpus during supplier scoring. Your first project will be re-architecting how those calls are made — batching, parallelizing, and caching intelligently on AWS — so the engine scales without linearly scaling cost or latency. From there, you'll expand into general infrastructure support across Trustbridge's other components (RFP/RFQ tooling, supplier assessment site, referral/payment tracking).
What You'll Work On

- Profile and diagnose the current historical-corpus query pattern in the matching engine to identify where serial calls can be parallelized or cached.

- Design and implement AWS-based solutions (e.g., Lambda concurrency, SQS/Step Functions for parallel fan-out, ElastiCache or DynamoDB caching layers) to reduce redundant repeat calls.

- Build monitoring and cost-visibility into scaling changes so improvements are measurable, not assumed.

- Partner with our Director of AI/ML Software Engineering to align infrastructure changes with the matching engine's scoring logic (corporate fit, capability profile, historical project corpus).

- Extend infrastructure practices to other Trustbridge components as the internship progresses.

- Support migration of existing workloads and services to AWS — assessing what to lift-and-shift vs. re-architect, planning data migration and cutovers, and validating performance and cost post-migration.

- Document architecture decisions and run books so improvements are maintainable beyond the internship.

What We're Looking For

We hire on four traits above all else, and we screen for them as rigorously as technical skill:

- Communication — clear speaking, writing, and listening, and a sense of timing for when to raise something.

- Hard work and reliability — you follow through and can be counted on.

- Willingness and ability to learn — genuine intellectual curiosity, not just credentials.

- Positive attitude — you bring people up, not down.

On the technical side:

- Solid programming fundamentals (any modern language; Python or Node.js a plus).

- Exposure to AWS core services (Lambda, EC2, S3, RDS/DynamoDB, SQS/SNS, or similar) through coursework, personal projects, or prior internships.

- Working knowledge of cloud migration concepts — lift-and-shift vs. re-platforming vs. re-architecting, data migration approaches, and minimizing downtime during cutover (exposure through coursework or projects is fine).

- Understanding of the difference between serial and parallel execution, and curiosity about caching strategies and when they apply.

- Comfortable working independently against written specs and asking sharp questions when specs are ambiguous.

How We Work

Trustbridge runs lean: a senior AI/ML engineering lead sets technical direction, and interns execute against clearly documented SOPs and specs with AI-assisted tooling in the loop. You'll have a daily touchpoint with our Chief of Staff and direct technical guidance from our senior engineering lead — you won't be thrown in without support, but you will be expected to own your workstream.
Details

•Location: India-based, full-time.

- Compensation: Paid stipend (details discussed during interview).

- Reports to: Director of AI/ML Software Engineering, with daily coordination through the Chief of Staff.

To Apply

Send your resume and a short note on a project where you parallelized, cached, or otherwise optimized something that was previously running serially — tell us what was slow, what you changed, and what got better.

title: Analytics - Future Leaders Graduate Program
description:
Real ownership. Real impact. Build from day one.

Are you an ambitious graduate ready to tackle complex , real-world challenges at the intersection of data, strategy and tech?

The Future Leaders Graduate Program – Business Analytics at Picnic is a two-year launchpad for exceptional talents. From day one, you join a business team, own a business topic, and become an expert in your field.

At Picnic, we’re building the future of grocery. Using cutting-edge technology and data-driven innovation, we challenge the status quo and build the world’s smartest, most customer-focused supermarket.
We move fast, think big, and turn bold ideas into tangible impact.

Tricks of the trade

- Lead with ambition : Bring your relentless determination, creativity, and grit. Take the driver’s seat and redefine the grocery shopping experience for millions. You will be expected to think independently, move fast, and deliver results.

- Steep learning curve : Your growth comes from owning real problems, testing your ideas, learning from your mistakes and starting again. You'll blend hands-on training with immediate execution, you’ll move at a pace that accelerates your growth like nowhere else.

- Solve real-life puzzles : Spot opportunities, use tools at the forefront of technology, and own the outcome end to end. Not just making slides, but building the solution yourself.

- Innovate across borders : You’ll collaborate with teams across the Netherlands, Germany, and France, tackling challenges that redefine how Picnic operates at a European scale.

- High-performance environment : You’ll work alongside some of the best teams in analytics and tech, people who set a high bar and expect you to do the same.

From learning to leading

Throughout the two-year program, you’ll own business-critical projects from start to finish, supported by mentorship, learning sessions, and regular feedback.

You’ll strengthen your leadership skills in project management, storytelling, stakeholder communication, and giving and receiving feedback, while sharpening your technical skills in Python, SQL, Excel, and PowerPoint.

As your scope grows, so does your responsibility. You might scale your initial project or take on new challenges within the same domain. Either way, the pace is yours to set, and there’s always a new challenge to lead and an opportunity to make an impact. That’s why every journey is unique: there’s no standardized path through the program, just continuous opportunities to learn, and lead.

Where you’ll make an impact

From day one, you’ll be embedded in a business team, taking ownership in one of the following domains:

- Consumer - Drive growth through pricing, supplier strategy, and our market strategy. Think: Shaping our successful market entry into new cities. Your decisions shape how millions of customers experience Picnic.

- Logistics - Build the backbone of Picnic: robotic fulfilment, demand forecasting, route optimization across Europe and much more

Your superpowers

You don't wait for permission. You see a problem, build the solution, and bring people with you, before anyone asks. You've probably already started something: a project, a product, a business, an initiative that didn't exist until you made it happen.

More specifically, you:

- Are about to graduate (or recently graduated) a Masters in a quantitative field

- Have experience in high-performance environments: consulting, fast-growth startups, or competitive internships.

- Show an entrepreneurial mindset : you build, improve, and take ownership without being asked

- Think like a builder : hands-on, curious, and driven to challenge the status quo with practical solutions

- You have already gained basic knowledge in PowerPoint, Python, SQL, Excel or alternative coding languages

- EU citizenship or valid EU working permit required .

Many strong candidates (particularly women) talk themselves out of applying because they don't tick every box. If this excites you and you believe you have what it takes, apply. We only hire when we find the right match. That’s why our selection process is intentionally highly selective.

Why Picnic?

- Grow as we grow . We’re scaling quickly across countries and millions of customers and this is just the start. Grow your impact as we grow; we invest in your path but the driver's seat is always yours.

- Work with other innovators.  Work with a driven, energetic team that builds, wins, and celebrates together (think of legendary Friday drinks, our Ski trip and our parties)

- Kickstart your career.  Earn a competitive salary and step into a program designed to launch your long-term future at Picnic.

When are you joining?

- Fall Edition 2026
Start dates: September, October
*earlier or later dates can be arranged, please indicate your preference in the application question

- Spring Edition 2027
Start dates: February, March
*earlier or later dates can be arranged, please indicate your preference in the application question

📍 Location: Full-time in Paris, with period trips to NL and DE

There is no deadline : Our aim is to find the most ambitious people out there. We onboard talents on a monthly basis, so whether you join in April or August, you’ll always have a group of people sharing the ride.

Picnic Perks

🚲Health and Transportation
Through our partnerships with Malakoff Humanis and OpenUp, you have the opportunity to enroll in our company health insurance plan, as well as free and easy access to professional psychologists, workshops, and practical tools. Additionally, if you commute to work using public transportation, we reimburse 50% of your subscription cost.

🍉Food
Since we are located in the center of Paris, there is no on-site cafeteria. However, you will receive meal vouchers worth €11 per day to explore all the delicious restaurants nearby. Our small kitchen is also stocked with tasty snacks and refreshments.

📈Personal and Professional Development
You will have the opportunity to develop your skills not only through exciting projects and a dynamic environment but also via training programs offered by Lepaya.

🏖️All the rest
You get 25 days of paid vacation, plus additional rest days (RTT) based on the number of days worked in the year. Picnic provides you with a laptop, a phone, and a paid SIM card.
🚀Access to exclusive deals and perks through our Works Council (CSE) and our partner Swile (gift cards, concert tickets, cinema discounts, and more)

FAQ

Do I need a quantitative background? It's a strong advantage, but not a hard requirement. If your internships and projects demonstrate real hands-on ownership and data-driven thinking, we'll consider your application. You do need a Master's degree, basic knowledge of Python or SQL, and relevant work experience.

Does the program include rotations? No, intentionally. We believe depth creates ownership, and ownership creates impact. Rather than rotating across teams, you’ll go deep in one area, build real expertise, and gradually expand your scope as your impact grows. If you have topic preferences, tell us during the process.

In what language should I apply? English. Please include your CV and Master's degree transcript or any other relevant test scores (e.g., GMAT)

What are the long-term opportunities after the program? This program is a fast track into a high-impact career at Picnic, it’s an entry point for a long-term future, not a two-year stopover.

Career paths here are as varied as the people on them. Some grow vertically, building deep expertise and a team around them as their project expands. Others move laterally - from Commercial to Fulfilment, Distribution to Customer, or wherever their strengths and ambitions take them. What they share is real ownership, real impact, and a career they shaped themselves.

title: IT System Engineer (m/w/d) – Projektgeschäft
description:
Projekte statt Tickets · Eimeldingen (Landkreis Lörrach), vor Ort und bei Kunden in der Region · Vollzeit · Professional oder Senior

Du kommst aus der Systemadministration oder bist schon System Engineer und willst Projekte umsetzen, statt Tickets abzuarbeiten? Dann bist Du bei uns vom ersten Kundentermin bis zum erfolgreichen Go-live dabei. Den laufenden Betrieb übernehmen danach unser Tagesgeschäft und unsere Managed Services. Am Ende weisst Du genau, was Du gebaut hast.

Das machst Du

- Analyse: Du nimmst die IT beim Kunden vor Ort auf und verschaffst Dir ein ehrliches Bild – auch wenn die Doku lückenhaft ist.

- Konzept: Du wählst herstellerneutral die passende Lösung und planst Architektur, Zeitplan, Risiken und Rollback, bevor Du etwas anfasst.

- Umsetzung: Du packst selbst an und stimmst Dich laufend mit Kunden, Softwareherstellern und Planungsbüros ab – keine Blackbox.

- Übergabe: Du dokumentierst so, dass andere ohne Rückfrage übernehmen können, und übergibst an den Kunden oder unsere Managed Services.

Professional oder Senior?

Als Senior verantwortest Du Projekte von Anfang an selbst und gibst Dein Wissen im Team weiter. Als Professional startest Du an der Seite erfahrener Teammitglieder und übernimmst Schritt für Schritt eigene Projekte. Wo Du einsteigst, klären wir offen im Gespräch.

Typische Projekte

Unsere Kunden kommen unter anderem aus Fertigung, Logistik, Gesundheitswesen und Bevölkerungsschutz.

- VMware → Proxmox: Umzug einer Serverlandschaft in unsere Cloud

- Umstieg von lokalem Active Directory auf Microsoft Entra ID – mit Profilmigration, Intune und Fileserver-Umzug nach SharePoint

- OPNsense-Firewall-Cluster mit Standortvernetzung per VPN

- Modernisierung kompletter IT-Infrastrukturen bei mittelständischen Betrieben inklusive Bestandsaufnahme, Konzeption, Budgetierung sowie Umsetzung

- Netzwerkplanung für einen Neubau , zusammen mit dem Planungsbüro

- Knifflige Fälle: Projekte, an denen andere gescheitert sind, oder gewachsene Umgebungen ohne Doku

Das bringst Du mit

- Mindestens zwei Jahre Praxis in Systemadministration oder IT-Betrieb – egal ob nach Ausbildung (z. B. Fachinformatiker·in für Systemintegration), Studium oder Quereinstieg

- Windows Server und Active Directory sicher im Griff: GPOs, DNS/DHCP, Berechtigungen, RDS

- Solides Netzwerk- und Firewall-Wissen: VLANs, Routing, VPN (z. B. OPNsense oder Sophos)

- Grundlagen der Microsoft-365-Administration: Benutzer, Lizenzen, Exchange Online, Teams und SharePoint

- Du erklärst technische Entscheidungen verständlich, auch der Geschäftsführung beim Kunden

- Sehr gutes Deutsch für Kundengespräche und Konzepte sowie Führerschein Klasse B für Kundentermine

Schön, aber kein Muss

- Proxmox/Ceph, VMware oder Hyper-V

- Entra ID, Intune und Conditional Access

- Linux, MikroTik oder PowerShell

- Erfahrung aus Migrationsprojekten

Du musst nicht alles mitbringen: Proxmox und Ceph bringen wir Dir bei – und wenn nicht jeder Punkt passt, freuen wir uns trotzdem auf Deine Bewerbung.

Warum layer7

Wir sind ein inhabergeführter Managed Service Provider aus dem Dreiländereck mit über 35 Leuten in Eimeldingen und Basel. Die drei Gründer führen das Unternehmen seit 2010 gemeinsam. Unsere Infrastruktur haben wir selbst in der Hand: eigene Hardware in drei Rechenzentren (Basel, Weil am Rhein, Frankfurt), eigenes Netzwerk und Peering, über 1.500 gemanagte Server.

- Attraktives Gehalt – leistungsgerechte Vergütung ohne negative Überraschungen

- Attraktive Bonusregelung – Dein Einsatz zahlt sich aus

- Firmenwagen – auch zur privaten Nutzung

- Weiterbildung nach Deiner Wahl – Du wählst Kurse und Zertifizierungen, wir zahlen Kurse und Prüfungen

- Dein Arbeitsgerät – Windows, Linux oder Mac: Du entscheidest

- Hansefit – Fitnessstudios, Schwimmbäder und mehr, für Gesundheit und Ausgleich

- Kurze Entscheidungswege – inhabergeführt, kein Konzernprozess

- Starkes Team – Zusammenhalt im Alltag und Teamevents vom Europa-Park bis zum Grillfest

So geht’s weiter

Bewerbung → Kennenlernen → Fachgespräch → Angebot. Schnelle Entscheidung, kein Konzernprozess. Die Online-Bewerbung dauert wenige Minuten, ohne Konto – ein Lebenslauf reicht.

title: Applied Scientist/Machine Learning Engineer, Gaia
description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Simulation Teams
Generative Simulation is the team advancing our end-to-end autonomous driving research, incubating and investing in new ideas that can become game-changing technological advances for Wayve. As a Machine Learning Engineer in the team, you will play a key role in developing next-generation world models and planners, such as GAIA, that can simulate complex, diverse, and temporally consistent driving environments to power faster training, broader testing, and scalable deployment, even in areas and scenarios we have never driven in before. As we push toward the next generation of GAIA, efficiency and interactivity are a major focus: models must run thousands of roll-outs per second, support closed-loop agent interaction, and fit within practical compute budgets. You will work at the intersection of machine learning research, multi-modal modelling, and real-world deployment, tackling questions such as how we can deploy autonomous vehicles in a new geography without collecting any real-world data, and whether synthetically generated environments can fully replace physical testing and data collection.

🧠 Your day-to-day

- Setting technical direction: Set technical direction and designing key components of the system.

- Deep work / coding: You spend a focused block implementing and debugging new modeling capabilities.

- Cross-team collaboration, brainstorming and pairing: you brainstorm ideas with your team mates or pair to solve a difficult problem

- Mentorship / async review: You review a teammate’s pull request or experimental design and outcomes and provide feedback

- Sync-ups: Share findings with the rest of your team leading to a discussion on designing the next experiments. You align on shared priorities for the week and blockers.

- Paper reading/ reading groups: Read one of the latest papers and summarise them for yourself or the team to present in the next reading group if interesting

🧩 What you’ll be working on

- Invent next-generation, efficient generative world-models (diffusion, transformer or hybrid) that deliver real-time roll-outs and controllable scene editing.

- Architect interactive world models where agents (or humans) can step the model, enabling reinforcement learning, planning and safety evaluation loops.

- Optimise end-to-end performance – from latent compression to context pruning – your aim is to reduce inference latency by orders of magnitude.

- Define robust metrics for long-horizon coherence, physics fidelity and planner integration; run ablations and scaling studies to understand trade-offs.

- Ship impact: integrate your models into closed-loop training and evaluation, and measure the sim-to-real gap against on-road driving-model results.

- Mentor and influence: guide junior researchers, shape technical road-maps, publish at top venues and represent Wayve in the community.

- Challenge assumptions and drive innovation: propose bold ideas, conduct ablation studies, and question conventional approaches to training and evaluation.

🙌 You should apply if

- 4+ years of experience in ML research/engineering with a focus on generative video, world models.

- Deep knowledge in diffusion & latent-video models; track record of improving sampling efficiency or model throughput.

- Experience working with high-dimensional temporal or spatial-temporal data (e.g., video, multi-sensor fusion).

- Strong Python and PyTorch engineering fundamentals, and experience building research-grade production tools.

- Strong publication record or contributions to open-source ML tooling.

- Ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced, innovative, interdisciplinary team environment.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More about Wayve:
🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.
Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:
Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process:
Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

- Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins)

- Competency Interviews (Programming/Pytorch debugging and hiring manager interview; 2 hours total)

- Deep-dive technical interviews (Systems & domain-specific interviews; 3 hours total)

- Final interview : Mission & values alignment (45 mins).

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):
💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more
A quick, honest note before you apply.
Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve

DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.

description:
Position Summary

We are looking for a Junior Web & AI Automation Developer to support an Australian business growth agency that helps small and medium-sized businesses connect their websites, online marketing, CRM systems, lead follow-up and practical AI automation.

The role will focus primarily on website implementation and maintenance, followed by CRM workflows and digital marketing configuration. Basic AI automation will be a smaller, developing part of the role. Working directly with the business owner, you will turn approved strategies, designs and content into functioning websites and connected systems.

This is a hands-on junior generalist position for someone with programming fundamentals, strong problem-solving skills and a willingness to learn. Much of the work will involve template configuration, content implementation, research and troubleshooting rather than extensive custom coding.

Job Details

Work Setup: Work from home

Shift/Schedule: Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Brisbane time, including a one-hour lunch break

Holidays: Australian public holidays, based on the holiday calendar provided by the client

Responsibilities

Website Development and Maintenance

- Build, update and maintain responsive websites and landing pages using Zoho Sites or other approved website builders, content management systems and low-code platforms.

- Implement approved templates, layouts, copy and images, maintaining consistent presentation and a mobile-friendly user experience.

- Make appropriate HTML, CSS and JavaScript adjustments, and troubleshoot layout, styling, scripting and website integration issues.

- Test pages, forms and links across common browsers and screen sizes. Check spelling, grammar and content accuracy, and support basic accessibility, loading performance and technical SEO improvements.

CRM Configuration and Integrations

- Configure CRM lead-capture and follow-up workflows using Zoho or a client's existing CRM platform.

- Connect website forms, CRMs, email platforms and other business systems using available integrations, APIs or webhooks, with guidance as needed.

- Populate workflows with supplied content, and test triggers, field mappings, actions and error handling to ensure information moves reliably between systems.

Digital Marketing Implementation

- Configure client accounts in Zoho Social or other approved marketing platforms, and upload and schedule content and graphics provided by the business owner.

- As responsibilities develop, assist with monitoring client systems, flag configuration or technical issues, and support client reporting as assigned.

Basic AI and Workflow Automation

- Support the setup and testing of simple, supervised AI assistants, agents and automations using approved tools and implementation guidance.

- Research unfamiliar tools and integrations, use AI-generated instructions as a starting point where appropriate, and apply programming logic to identify gaps and troubleshoot issues.

- Contribute to internal AI and automation projects during quieter client-delivery periods to help reduce repetitive work and improve internal processes.

- Test outputs, follow agreed access controls and retain human review and approval before automations or AI tools are used operationally.

Documentation, Quality and Collaboration

- Document website changes, system configurations, workflows, dependencies, testing and basic handover or recovery steps.

- Follow procedures for protecting passwords, API keys and client data, and obtain the business owner's approval before production releases.

- Communicate progress, questions, blockers and delays promptly, and incorporate feedback to improve the quality and reliability of your work.

Qualifications

3 years of relevant commercial experience in web development, website implementation or a related technical role involving website work.

Essential Capabilities

- A practical programming background and working knowledge of HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with the ability to understand, adapt and troubleshoot website code.

- Hands-on experience with website builders, content management systems or low-code platforms, such as Zoho Sites, WordPress or comparable tools.

- Ability to diagnose website issues and test changes across common browsers and screen sizes.

- An understanding of APIs, webhooks, JSON and how websites exchange information with other systems, together with a willingness to learn unfamiliar integrations.

- Basic understanding of AI tools and a genuine interest in learning practical automation and AI-assisted implementation. Advanced AI engineering experience is not required.

- Strong written and spoken English, including the ability to identify spelling, grammar and content errors when implementing websites and workflows.

- Strong logical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to research unfamiliar tasks, ask questions and work through gaps in instructions.

- A reliable, organised and detail-oriented approach, with the ability to follow documented procedures, protect confidential information and respond constructively to feedback.

- A fast, reliable internet connection and availability to work the agreed Brisbane business-hours schedule.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with Zoho applications, particularly Zoho Sites, CRM, Forms, Flow, Creator, Campaigns or Social. Zoho experience is advantageous but not mandatory.

- Exposure to automation platforms such as Make, Zapier, n8n or Zoho Flow, including simple workflow or system-integration projects.

- Experience configuring CRM follow-up workflows, form-to-CRM connections or digital marketing platforms.

- Examples of practical AI-enabled applications, assistants, integrations or agents, including small personal or learning projects.

- Familiarity with conversion-focused page design, technical SEO, secure credential management or related website quality practices.

- Experience supporting Australian, New Zealand, United Kingdom or United States clients.

Portfolio and Work Samples

Candidates are encouraged to share available website examples, code samples or related implementation work and explain their personal contribution. Alternative examples can be discussed where confidentiality limits sharing. Automation and AI work samples are welcome but are not mandatory.

title: Infrastructure Software Engineer
description:
Join our mission
We're proud to work with many incredible companies, accelerating their ability to build their products.
We've spent years watching talented engineering teams lose momentum to the same frustrating bottleneck: waiting. Waiting for CI to finish. Waiting for builds to complete. Waiting for tests to run.
After experiencing this pain firsthand at companies of every size, we set out to build the developer infrastructure platform we'd always wanted to use. Something that would seamlessly integrate with our workflows and the tools teams already love—but make everything dramatically faster and more cost-effective.
Today, we're already accelerating hundreds of companies around the world, helping them ship features instead of waiting for infrastructure. We've built something that feels almost magical in its simplicity: change your runs-on line, mount your toolchain cache directory and suddenly your builds are 5x faster.
About the role
Namespace's approach is low-friction, designed for immediate integration into existing developer toolchains, empowering teams to experience tangible results within just five minutes. With an end-to-end stack optimized for high performance—including compute, memory, storage, and networking—Namespace delivers capabilities and efficiencies unmatched by traditional cloud providers.
Own the software that drives our hardware. You'll write the control planes, automation, and observability that keep our global fleet fast, efficient, and reliable, while charting a path to scale that continues to increase the number of "machines under management" per engineer.
Our culture
We're looking for people with grit—people who push through ambiguity, take ownership, and keep going when things get hard. You're deeply curious, driven to understand how things work and how they can be improved. Most importantly, you have a strong bias to execution: you don't wait for perfect conditions, you ship, learn, and iterate quickly. If you care about building, moving fast, and making real impact, you'll fit right in.

What you'll do

- Manage and automate the fleet – build services for provisioning, health checks, upgrades, and incident remediation

- Uphold reliability – embed observability, graceful degradation, and rollback paths into every layer you touch

- Architect the network – design and evolve a high-throughput, low-latency fabric tailored to our high performance use-cases

- Ship software, not scripts – develop clean, testable code (mostly Go) that treats our fleet like a first-class API

- Drive efficiency – improve utilization and power-to-performance ratios so capacity grows slower than usage

- Partner across the stack – work with product, infra, and platform teams to scope and deliver features like storage-aware scheduling, cache volumes, and other developer-facing features

What we're looking for

- Proven experience engineering large-scale infrastructure - writing the software that runs fleets, not just operating existing hyperscalers

- Depth in network architecture, data-center design, and performance tuning

- Hands-on time deploying and managing compute hardware at scale (servers, switches, etc)

- Fluency with modern orchestration and automation tooling (Kubernetes, Terraform, Ansible - plus the judgment to know when to build vs. buy)

- A track record of delivering reliable systems and measurable efficiency gains

You can expect:

- Competitive salary and stock options

- Flexible working hours

- Market-leading parental leave

Life at Namespace Labs:

- We pride ourselves in being a small team of experts that can achieve a lot.

- We balance our long-term vision with short-term pragmatism.

- We believe in being fully transparent internally on how decisions are made, on how the company is doing, and we use that information to drive our decisions.

title: Solutions Engineer, Payments Infrastructure
description:
OVERVIEW
Formance builds programmable financial infrastructure. Our open-source ledger helps engineering teams model, track, and reconcile money movements across financial products, from payment platforms to fintech applications and digital-asset businesses.
Financial infrastructure requires precision. Teams need to understand where money is, how it moves, and whether their systems reflect what actually happened. We build the tools to help them answer those questions.

YOUR ROLE
We’re looking for a Solutions Engineer with a strong technical foundation and experience in fintech or payments to join our team.
You’ll work with prospective customers to understand their architecture, map their financial flows, and demonstrate how Formance fits their requirements. You’ll partner closely with our sales, product, and engineering teams throughout the evaluation process.
This role combines technical depth with commercial judgment. You should be comfortable building a proof of concept, discussing architectural tradeoffs with an engineer, and explaining the business implications to a founder.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Lead technical discovery with engineering and product teams to understand their financial workflows, constraints, and evaluation criteria.

- Build tailored demos and proofs of concept using Formance’s APIs and tooling.

- Guide technical evaluations, investigate questions, and help prospects assess product fit.

- Partner with sales to connect technical capabilities to business needs and move opportunities forward.

- Bring customer feedback to product and engineering, with concrete examples of gaps and recurring needs.

REQUIREMENTS

- Experience in fintech, payments, banking infrastructure, or digital-asset infrastructure. You understand how money moves through a financial product and the operational challenges involved.

- A strong technical foundation. You can work with APIs, read and write code, debug integrations, and reason about data models and system architecture.

- Experience working directly with customers , through solutions engineering, solutions architecture, technical consulting, or an engineering role with significant customer exposure.

- The ability to ask precise questions, uncover requirements, and explain complex concepts clearly.

- Commercial judgment: you understand how a technical evaluation contributes to a buying decision.

- A hands-on approach and the ability to work independently in a small team.

- Strong written and spoken English, with the ability to lead technical conversations with international customers.

Useful additional experience

- Working with ledgers, double-entry accounting, reconciliation, or payment orchestration.

- Supporting technical evaluations for API-first or developer-facing products.

- Building financial workflows involving multiple currencies, payment providers, or digital assets.

- Turning recurring customer questions into reusable demos, documentation, or tools.

WHY JOIN FORMANCE?
You’ll work directly with teams building financial products and help them make consequential infrastructure decisions.
You’ll have ownership of technical evaluations, close access to product and engineering, and the opportunity to shape how we demonstrate and explain Formance. Your work will influence both customer decisions and the product we build.

BENEFITS

- Flexible remote work policy

- Health insurance: Alan Blue, with your partner and dependent children covered at no cost from day one.

- Meal vouchers: €10 per day worked, with 55% covered by Formance.

- Equipment: A MacBook from day one, plus a €500 onboarding budget for your workspace equipment.

- Parenthood support: Formance maintains 100% of your salary during the first month of additional birth leave.

- Company offsite: An annual company offsite, fully organized and covered by Formance.

title: Platform Engineer, AI Enablement
description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Engineering Teams
Wayve’s AI Enablement team builds the shared platforms that help people across the company use language models and AI agents safely, reliably, and cost-effectively. As an early member of this platform team, you’ll help shape both the technical foundations and the standards for how AI-powered tools are built and operated across Wayve.

🧠 Your day-to-day
You’ll design, build, and operate infrastructure for model access, agent runtimes, and observability. You’ll take projects from initial problem definition through technical design, deployment, and ongoing operation, partnering closely with security, IT, and engineering teams. You’ll also support teams adopting the platform by troubleshooting issues, documenting reusable patterns, and helping people understand what’s possible with the tools available.

🧩 What you’ll be working on

- A governed, production-ready access layer for language models, including routing, authentication, cost controls, and auditability.

- Secure infrastructure and reusable tooling for running agentic workflows in production.

- Observability covering platform usage, cost, reliability, and performance.

- Governance and safety controls that make AI use secure, compliant, and auditable.

- Shared primitives, standards, and best practices that enable teams to build and deploy agents without creating one-off infrastructure.

- Reliable, scalable deployments using cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, and infrastructure-as-code.

🙌 You should apply if

- You have strong software engineering experience building APIs, services, or developer tooling.

- You’ve built or operated platforms and infrastructure used by other engineering teams.

- You have hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, and infrastructure-as-code.

- You’re familiar with LLM APIs and the surrounding ecosystem, such as model gateways, agent frameworks, MCP, or RAG.

- You understand production observability, including metrics, tracing, and logging.

- You take a security-conscious approach to authentication, authorization, governance, and auditability.

- You’re comfortable taking ownership in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment and can communicate clearly through documentation and collaboration.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More about Wayve:
🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.
Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:
Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process:
Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

- Recruiter screen

- Competency Interviews

- Deep-dive technical interviews

- Final interview : mission & values alignment

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):
💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more
A quick, honest note before you apply.
Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve

DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.

title: MCP & Memory Intern
description:
Job Description:
DataRobot delivers AI that maximizes impact and minimizes business risk. Our platform and applications integrate into core business processes so teams can develop, deliver, and govern AI at scale. DataRobot empowers practitioners to deliver predictive and generative AI, and enables leaders to secure their AI assets. Organizations worldwide rely on DataRobot for AI that makes sense for their business — today and in the future.
This effort is about making AI agents more useful in real work: giving them the right tools, the right context, and a memory that holds up across a conversation and across sessions. The focus is Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent memory, how an agent discovers tools, calls them safely, keeps track of what it has learned, and stays helpful without someone watching every step. The goal is practical value for people using agents day to day, with clean implementations that others can build on.

Summary:

This is a hands-on internship for someone curious about AI agents who wants to learn by building. You do not need to already be an expert. What matters is that you like figuring things out, you move without waiting to be told every next step, and you care about unblocking the people around you. Most of the work sits on MCP and memory: connecting agents to tools, shaping how context is passed in, and designing how an agent remembers what is useful and forgets what is not. You will write code, try ideas, see what breaks, and ship improvements in a fast-moving environment. A good attitude and the willingness to learn matter more than a perfect resume.

Required Skills:

- Comfort writing and reading Python, and a willingness to get better at it quickly.

- Curiosity about how AI agents work: tools, prompts, context windows, and why an agent succeeds or fails on a real task.

- Interest in MCP — how servers expose tools, how clients call them, and how that contract stays simple and reliable.

- Interest in memory for agents: what to store, what to retrieve, and how that changes what the agent can do next.

- Ability to take a vague problem, try a small version, and show what you learned.

- Clear communication: you say when you are stuck, you share what you tried, and you help other people move faster.

- Good engineering habits you are willing to practice: readable code, small tests, and notes so the next person is not lost.

- You take feedback on board. When someone points out a better approach, a mistake, or a simpler path, use it and adjust.

Strong Plus:

- You have built or used an MCP server or client, even a small one.

- You have played with agent frameworks or tool calling.

- You have thought about memory, caching, or conversation state in any product, not only in AI.

- You enjoy fast environments and would rather try something today than wait for a perfect plan.

- You like helping teammates get unblocked, even when the task is not yours.

What You Can Expect To Work On:

- Building and improving MCP servers and clients: tool definitions, inputs and outputs, error handling, and examples other people can run.

- Experimenting with agent memory: what gets saved, how it is retrieved, and how that changes task quality.

- Wiring tools and memory into an agent loop and watching where it gets confused, slow, or wrong.

- Making small, clear changes that unblock teammates - docs, fixtures, smoke tests, and fixes that remove friction.

- Turning a rough idea into something that runs, then tightening it based on what you see.

- Pairing with people who know the system well, then owning the next slice yourself.

What You Should Expect:

- Work close to how agents actually get used, with MCP and memory at the center.

- A fast pace: short loops, quick feedback, and room to try things without a long approval chain.

- Trust to drive your own tasks once the goal is clear. You will not be micro-managed.

- A team that likes curiosity, a steady attitude, and people who make others faster.

- Room to learn in public: questions are welcome, and “I don’t know yet” is a fine starting point if you go find out.

- A role for someone who wants to grow into agentic systems by shipping, not by waiting until they feel fully ready.

The talent and dedication of our employees are at the core of DataRobot ’s journey to be an iconic company. We strive to attract and retain the best talent by providing competitive pay and benefits with our employees’ well-being at the core. Here’s what your benefits package may include depending on your location and local legal requirements: Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance, Flexible Time Off Program, Paid Holidays, Paid Parental Leave, Global Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and more!

title: Go-to-Market Engineer (m/w/d)
description:
Wir bauen die Software, mit der WEG- und Mietverwaltungen ihren Alltag rechtssicher und ohne Medienbrüche organisieren, umfangreich und modern, aber erschwinglich, für das digitale Zeitalter der Immobilienwirtschaft. Die Immobilienverwaltung zählt zu den analogsten Branchen in Deutschland, genau das wollen wir ändern.

Unser Team kombiniert Erfahrung aus dem Verwalteralltag mit dem IT-Know-how eines innovativen Tech-Unternehmens. Seit unserer Gründung 2020 sind wir aus der Praxis für die Praxis gewachsen. Wir sind ein Team von 26 Menschen in Brühl bei Köln, das Verantwortung ernst nimmt und Entscheidungen schnell trifft.

Wir wachsen und mit uns die Anforderungen an unsere Infrastruktur über Marketing, Vertrieb und Customer Success hinweg. Dafür suchen wir keine Person, die HubSpot verwaltet, sondern jemanden, der sie baut: Strukturen, Automatisierungen und Tracking, die den gesamten Weg vom ersten Kontakt bis zur langfristigen Kundenbeziehung sauber abbilden. Du berichtest direkt an unsere CRO.

Aufgaben

- Du übernimmst HubSpot als zentrale Infrastruktur für Marketing, Vertrieb und Customer Success und baust Strukturen, die mit unserem Wachstum mitskalieren.

- Du entwickelst Automatisierungen, die manuelle Arbeit aus unseren Teams herausnehmen, von Content-Automatisierung über Lead-Routing bis zu automatisierten Abläufen im Customer Success, etwa beim Onboarding neuer Kund:innen.

- Du baust mit n8n oder vergleichbaren Low-Code-Tools Workflows, die Systeme miteinander verbinden, die bisher nebeneinander laufen.

- Du setzt KI gezielt dort ein, wo sie echten Mehrwert bringt: bei Recherche, Optimierung, Datenanreicherung oder Content-Erstellung.

- Bei Bedarf baust du auch mal eine Landingpage in Webflow oder ein Tracking-Setup, das uns zeigt, was auf dem Weg zum Kunden tatsächlich funktioniert.

- Du arbeitest eng mit Marketing, Vertrieb und Customer Success zusammen und verstehst deren Prozesse gut genug, um sie in Systeme zu übersetzen, die im Alltag wirklich helfen.

Qualifikation

- Gute bis sehr gute HubSpot-Kenntnisse: Du hast bereits Strukturen aufgebaut, nicht nur gepflegt, und weißt, wie Workflows, Properties und Automatisierungen zusammenspielen.

- Fortgeschrittene Erfahrung mit Automatisierung über Low-Code- oder No-Code-Tools wie n8n.

title: Software Engineer, Robot Autonomy (Reliability & Test Infrastructure)
description:
Our Mission
At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient.
We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today!

The Role
You will own the path a code change takes from commit to robot, and the evidence behind every gate on that path. Today the honest answer to "is this build safe?" is "it worked on the test robot." You will replace that with a system: the simulation environment the team tests against, the regression suites that run on every change, the hardware-in-the-loop rigs, and the release gates that decide whether a build can go onto a robot that will patrol a customer site alone tonight.
This is the first engineer dedicated to reliability and test infrastructure, and it sits in our Robot Autonomy team, next to the engineers building perception, localisation, planning and locomotion. Our robots patrol security sites, critical infrastructure and defence facilities without a human present, so a bad release is not a rollback: it is a customer incident. Within six months, nothing should reach a customer robot without passing something you built.

What You'll Work On

- Release pipeline: code change, automated tests, simulation at scale, staging robot, pilot site, full rollout, with explicit pass criteria at every gate and nothing advancing without meeting them.

- Simulation as infrastructure: a GPU-backed simulation environment (Isaac Sim today) running continuously, so engineers test against scenarios instead of queueing for the one robot in the lab.

- Scenario libraries and regression suites: coverage across the whole on-robot stack, perception through locomotion, and the infrastructure to run thousands of scenarios on every change.

- Hardware-in-the-loop: bench rigs and test procedures on the physical robots for what simulation cannot tell you.

- Failure injection: drop sensors, degrade LiDAR returns, kill the network link, corrupt odometry, then verify the system degrades and recovers the way we tell customers it does.

- Field incidents to tests: when a robot misbehaves on site, reproduce it deterministically and turn it into a permanent regression test.

- Reproducibility: log capture, replay tooling, deterministic seeds, versioned scenarios, and coverage metrics that are honest about what they do not cover.

- Acceptance criteria: turn product and customer requirements into measurable tests, and report against them without softening the numbers.

Who We're Looking For
A test, validation or reliability engineer who has shipped a product where failure had consequences, and who has seen what changes when a fleet goes from one unit to fifty. You treat simulation and CI as production infrastructure that you own, not tools you consume. You have judgment about what is worth testing: we want a safety net, not a wall of green ticks that hides the real risk. And you are comfortable being the person who says a build is not going out.

Your Background

- 4+ years in test, validation, reliability, SRE or platform engineering on a product that shipped to customers.

- Experience with a complex system at scale: autonomous driving, drones, industrial automation, medical devices or similar.

- Strong Python and/or C++, with solid CI/CD and containerised infrastructure skills.

- Hands-on with a robotics simulator run as production infrastructure: Isaac Sim preferred, Gazebo, MuJoCo or equivalent accepted.

- Comfortable owning cloud infrastructure and GPU orchestration, not just consuming it.

- Enough hardware literacy to read a timing problem or a flaky sensor trace, and the judgment to know when to hand it to Hardware.

Nice to Have

- ROS 2.

- Hardware-in-the-loop rigs and bench automation.

- Fleet telemetry and observability (Grafana, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry).

- Functional safety or comparable standards work.

- On-prem, air-gapped or defence deployment experience.

- Having been on call for hardware in the field.

What We Offer

- Ownership: you are able to ship products and deliver project end-to-end.

- Mission: autonomous security that keeps people and critical sites safe, including in defence.

- Career path: a ground-floor seat with real runway. Prove your value and you will not have barriers to grow.

- Team: work directly with PhD-level co-founders in AI, Robotics, and Physics, alongside a strong (and fun) founding team.

- Compensation: Competitive equity/salary package

- Culture: International founding team that is serious about building but does not take itself too seriously.

title: Growth Director

Compliance remains one of the most manual functions in financial services. While most institutions still rely on fragmented tools and human-driven workflows, we believe AI is enabling a fundamental shift toward autonomous compliance. We recently raised our Series A from leading US and European investors and software operators. We’re now entering our next chapter: investing heavily in product and AI, expanding internationally, and building the team that can make Dotfile the global standard for compliance infrastructure.

Role Overview
We are looking for a highly analytical, technical and hands-on Director of Growth to build and scale Dotfile’s growth engine.
You will own how we identify target accounts, capture buying signals, reach the right people with the right message, experiment with new channels, and turn what works into scalable systems. You will work closely with Marketing and Sales to generate qualified pipeline across our key markets, with a particular focus on our expansion in the US.
This is a builder role. You will combine strong growth instincts with data, automation and AI to build workflows for account research, enrichment, segmentation, personalization, campaign execution and analysis. You will own the full experimentation loop: finding opportunities, launching experiments quickly, measuring their impact on pipeline and revenue, and scaling the ones that work.
You will be expected to remain deeply hands-on with the tools and systems behind our growth engine. We want to build a small, highly leveraged growth team where technology replaces repetitive work and allows us to experiment faster and operate at greater scale.
You will report directly to the VP of Marketing.

Key Responsibilities

- Own Dotfile’s growth strategy and pipeline generation across our key markets, working closely with Marketing and Sales

- Build systems to identify target accounts and buying signals, enrich them with relevant data, and turn them into actionable growth opportunities

- Design and execute highly targeted outbound and account-based campaigns across channels, using AI and automation to operate at scale without sacrificing relevance

- Build workflows and agents for research, enrichment, segmentation, personalization, campaign execution and analysis

- Develop a high-velocity experimentation engine: identify new audiences, messages, channels and tactics, launch tests quickly, measure their impact and scale what works

- Own the growth stack and connect our CRM, data providers, automation tools, AI models and other systems to continuously improve how we generate pipeline

- Own growth analytics and performance, developing a clear understanding of funnel conversion, pipeline contribution, CAC and channel effectiveness

- Partner closely with Sales and Marketing to turn learnings from prospects, customers and campaign performance into better targeting, messaging and go-to-market decisions

About you

- You have 5+ years of experience in Growth, Growth Engineering, Demand Generation, Marketing Operations or another highly analytical role in B2B SaaS

- You have a track record of building growth programs that generated measurable pipeline and revenue, not just traffic, leads or engagement

- You are technically strong and comfortable working with data, APIs, webhooks, CRM systems, enrichment providers and automation tools

- AI is already part of how you work. You use LLMs and agents to research, build, analyze and execute, and naturally look for new things to automate

- You are a builder. You are comfortable connecting tools, creating workflows, manipulating data and prototyping solutions yourself rather than relying on others to do it for you

- You combine strong growth intuition with analytical rigor and can move comfortably between an idea, a dataset, an experiment and its impact on pipeline

- You thrive in a fast-moving environment with high standards and strong ownership. You are comfortable building from scratch, running multiple experiments in parallel and quickly changing direction when the data tells you to

- Experience growing an enterprise B2B SaaS business internationally, particularly in the US, is a plus

The interview process
Round 1: First conversation to get to know you, understand what drives you, and explore why this role excites you.
Round 2: Two-part discussion where you’ll walk us through your career journey and the choices that shaped it, followed by a values-based interview.
Round 3: Deep dive into one of your key projects with someone from a different team, offering a fresh, cross-functional perspective on how you work.
Round 4: Practical exercise, case study tailored to the role, giving you the opportunity to showcase your skills on a real-world challenge.
Round 5: Final conversation with our founder.
